title: Provision the club's tournament provider and administrator automatically
description: A working stack still needs CourtHive-side setup that today is done by hand with scripts and copied tokens. When an administrator switches Tournaments on, the app performs it against the local tournament server using the server's provisioner interface: it signs short-lived tokens as the instance service account with the tournament server's signing secret, creates a provisioner named jim-dot-tennis and the club's provider owned by it, creates the permanent never-used 'instance' provider administrator, records the provisioner and provider ids, and registers the provider in the app so calendar sync works immediately. No person receives a tournament credential: people reach tournament management through the hand-over in WI-152. The step is safe to repeat.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Cross-system provisioning with idempotency and credential handling.

acceptance_criteria: Switching Tournaments on in a fresh instance results in a provider, a tournament administrator and a registered provider record, with no command-line step
Running the step again changes nothing and reports the existing state
Tournament sync from the app works immediately afterwards and an empty calendar shows a helpful 'create your first tournament' pointer
Failures (server not ready) are reported with a retry, leaving no half-created state
`jim-dot-tennis tournaments provision` offers the same from the server
No tournament credential is created for or shown to any person; the app stores no API key (it signs its own short-lived tokens)
Tokens the app signs live 60 seconds, are never logged and never leave the server
Responses that report 'already exists' (HTTP 201 with error codes ABBREVIATION_EXISTS, SSO_IDENTITY_EXISTS, EMAIL_EXISTS) are treated as existing state when repeating

notes: The tournament server has a seed-admin script and a provider API; use its supported interfaces, not direct database writes.
Tokens copied from browsers have been truncated in the past - generate and pass credentials programmatically.
See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (WI-142, 2026-11-22): mechanism and exact calls are in section 4; all were run against the unmodified server image.

testing_requirements: Integration test against the tournament server image

context.user_story: As a club administrator, I want tournaments to be ready to use the moment I turn them on.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
